chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim asked about the waiting period of the woman with irregular menstruation (mustahadha), and he said:

"She waits for the duration of her usual menstrual period, or subtracts one day. If she does not menstruate, let her look to some of the women (of similar age/constitution) and count according to their menstrual period."

key_terms.بَعْضِ نِسَائِهَا: Some of the women (referring to peers for comparison)

ai.seo_question: How does a Shia Muslim woman determine her menstrual waiting period if she has irregular bleeding (istihadah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fiqh of *istihadha* (irregular bleeding), where the Imam instructs the woman to observe her habitual cycle or, if unknown, the pattern of other women, reflecting the Shia reliance on *'urf* (customary practice) in legal derivation. It highlights the methodological principle of using analogical comparison when specific physiological data is absent, ensuring the validity of her *iddah* for remarriage or prayer. This ruling underscores the practical application of flexibility within the structured framework of Shia jurisprudence regarding women's purity laws.
